title: Diagnose and recover RabbitMQ worker backlog
trigger: Queue depth is increasing while the RabbitMQ broker is healthy and at least one worker consumer remains connected.
preconditions: confirm the queue is durable and customer work is still being accepted
capture queue depth, ready/unacknowledged counts, consumer count, and worker runtime identity before mitigation
confirm whether worker processing is succeeding, failing, or absent
check for recent workload, configuration, dependency-latency, or release changes
diagnostic_steps: sample queue depth over time rather than relying on one snapshot
compare arrival volume with worker completion progress
confirm consumer count and worker health
inspect worker success/failure metrics and correlated logs
check API, PostgreSQL, Redis, and RabbitMQ health
distinguish sustained successful-but-slow processing from QW-001 consumer loss and QW-002 retry failure
mitigation_steps: remove only a confirmed temporary throughput constraint when that action is within L2 authority
do not restart a healthy worker merely because queue depth is high
do not purge durable customer work to make queue metrics look healthy
if sustained demand exceeds available capacity, escalate for approved worker scaling or performance remediation
validation_steps: queue depth trends down and reaches the expected steady state
all original affected customer work reaches completed processing state
worker success processing continues without new failure signal
API and dependency health remain normal
worker/API runtime identities remain unchanged when recovery did not require restart or redeployment
escalation_boundary: Escalate when backlog persists after the confirmed constraint is removed, sustained arrival rate exceeds supported capacity, worker success rate drops, failures appear, scaling or code/config changes are required, or customer work cannot be safely drained within the incident objective.
